findings: Size buckets and first4096bytes gate MD5 comparison for large files; no final byte comparison, no identity/mutation revalidation.
Small-file comparison reads cached size only without checking EOF, allowing later growth to remain undetected.
Nonfatal read errors can leave empty/stale byte buffers and proceed to equality test; needs isolated runtime reproduction.
compare_first_4k checks source buffer length twice, never validates second buffer length.
MD5 recomputed for every candidate pair, no digest cache; worst case repeated full reads. No benchmark performed.
Directory overlap uses lexical startswith, so sibling names like /a and /ab rejected and aliases not resolved.
Walks have no onerror callback and symlinks skipped; hardlink aliases not explicitly separated, no cancellation or complete/partial status.
Destructive commands read as source only, never executed.
Fixture-contained thirdparty Python test files must not be counted as library tests solely from path names.
Reproduced: stale cached size accepts longer candidate sharing original prefix.
Reproduced: two missing small files return duplicate=True when errors nonfatal. Empty existing source plus missing candidate also returns duplicate=True.
Reproduced: short second prefix read returnsFalse rather than required length error; healthy suffix difference is rejected by MD5 control.
Setup pytest runner explicitly excludes test_data; embedded thirdparty tests are byte fixtures, not Filegardener regression suite.
Root tests/test_basics.py AST inventory counts79test functions before parameter expansion, not executed cases. First250lines read; includes a no-assertion duplicate test and tautological examples.
README recommends nonfatal only-copy scanning; reproduced unreadable/missing false equality can hide a last copy under that policy.
Root MIT2016license read; setup classifier says Other/Proprietary, an inconsistent metadata label.

CI declares Python2.7/3.4/3.5/3.6 era matrix; declarations not passing evidence.
